chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa', from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Baseer, who said:
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) recited to me the obligatory inheritance shares of Ali (peace be upon him). Most of them were from five, or from four, and the majority of them were from six shares.

key_terms.أَسْهُمٍ: Shares/portions; the units used to divide an estate among heirs
key_terms.أَكْثَرُهُنَّ: Most of them (feminine plural); referring to the majority of inheritance cases
key_terms.فَرَائِضَ: Obligatory shares of inheritance (farā'id); the divinely prescribed portions in Islamic inheritance law

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the inheritance shares of Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Abu Baseer reports that Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) personally recited to him the system of obligatory inheritance shares (farā'id) established by Imam Ali (peace be upon him). The Imam explained that most inheritance cases are resolved from a base of five or four shares, while the largest common denominator used is six shares. This narration preserves an early Shia jurisprudential tradition on how inheritance fractions are calculated according to the Imamic teaching, reflecting the classical Islamic principle that inheritance shares must not exceed six as the least common multiple of all Quranic fractions.
